Consider the circle of radius $12$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$  traverse the circle once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(12,0)?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ generate a circle of radius $\frac{1}{2}$ centered at the origin?
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a circle  of radius $r$  centered at  the origin are

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, the radius $r=\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the circle are 

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
